column3: The Hebrew describes making a bald patch between your eyes.
The Hebrew joins the two introductory classes with “and”.
The Hebrew changes to plural possessives in the prohibitions about their meat and their carcass.
The field is singular, and the Hebrew explicitly mentions the produce of your seed.
The final blessing clause says “when the LORD your God blesses you,” rather than identifying the tithe as that with which He has blessed you.
The Hebrew describes binding up the silver in your hand.
The Hebrew twice makes the soul the subject of desiring or asking.
The Hebrew explicitly calls for the entire tithe of that year’s produce.
The blessing is introduced as a purpose, and your hand is singular.
